chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Lips Rose and the singer-director Edith Curry
summary: Alto player Lips Rose in Louisiana and his wife Edith, an opera-trained singer who fronted and directed the band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: But the radio was the big thing, radio and records -- the 78's, you know. I heard lots of, lots of great things go down, and I heard lots of great players when I would go out of town with the band during the summer. I remember an alto saxophone player named Lips(?) Rose; he was down in Alexandria, Louisiana -- great saxophone player. And his wife's name was Edith Kirk(?) They would work with a band called Little Joe. And she was a fantastic singer, had been opera-trained and everything, had a great presentation and everything. This lady was like a goddess. Edith Curry sang in front of that band, and she directed the band. You know, she did her trip in front of the band. Because there were
women doing it, like Blanche Calloway and Harriet Calloway. The band had the directors out there, you know...
